name: CapCut Font Shift Loop
use_when: A word or phrase should feel unstable, trendy, stylish, or rapidly expressive.
A hook or beat benefits from a brief font-change accent.
The edit can return to a stable base font before the viewer needs normal reading.
avoid_when: Continuous captions or accessibility subtitles need stable type.
The subject tone is serious or the changing fonts would feel gimmicky.
The loop would continue across multiple ideas and make hierarchy unclear.

timeline_pattern.pattern: base_text_layer -> blade_at_shift_start -> animation_loop_font_change -> optional_second_blade_new_font_loop -> final_blade_deselect_loop -> stable_font_hold
timeline_pattern.scope_rule: Blade only the section that should shift fonts; the rest of the text should keep the base style.
timeline_pattern.return_rule: Deselect the loop when the word should return to the original font lane.
timeline_pattern.sound_rule: Optional ticking SFX should end with the final font-change frame.

motion.rule: Font changes should be short bursts, not the default state of a readable caption system.

keyframe_values.duration: Use the shortest loop duration that lets the viewer understand the word.
keyframe_values.segments: Use separate blade cuts for different font-change loops only when each segment has a reason.
keyframe_values.stable_hold: Hold the final readable font after the loop so the word resolves.

sound.rule: Ticking SFX can sell font changes only when synced and kept below dialogue.

captions.rule: Do not use font-shift loops on ordinary subtitles; use them on designed emphasis text or title words.

color.rule: Keep color stable during the font loop unless the color change also has a meaning job.

implementation.ffmpeg: Approximate with rapid cuts between rendered text layers using different font files; keep final stable text onscreen.
implementation.remotion: Cycle fontFamily values across a short frame range, then lock to the final base or accent font with explicit finalHoldFrames.
implementation.blender: Swap text object font data or cut between text objects with different fonts, then hold the final object.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Blade the text where the shift begins, use Animation > Loop font-change presets on that segment, blade again for another loop if needed, then blade and deselect Loop to return to the original font.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Cut the text layer into short segments with different fonts or use a MOGRT/AE preset, then hold a final stable font.

common_mistakes: Leaving the font loop active after the emphasis beat ends.
Using too many font styles until the word loses identity.
Adding ticking SFX that continues after the visual shift.
Using font shift on small or dense captions.
Changing fonts without a tone, emphasis, or beat reason.
qc: Is the shifting word still readable through the loop?
Does the loop stop and resolve to a stable font?
Does any tick SFX end with the visual shift and stay below speech?
Does the font change support a real emphasis or tone shift?
Are ordinary captions suppressed or kept separate so they do not compete?
